question: What product will be formed when ethanol at 443K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid is heated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethene and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When ethanol is heated at 443K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, it undergoes a dehydration reaction.
 
• The dehydration of ethanol results in the formation of ethene (C₂H₄) and water (H₂O).
 
• Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent in this reaction.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dehydration Reaction:**

 
 
• A type of chemical reaction that involves the loss of water from the reacting molecule.
 
• In organic chemistry, it is commonly used to convert alcohols to alkenes.
 
 
 
• **Role of Sulphuric Acid:**
 
 
• Concentrated sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) is used as a catalyst and dehydrating agent in the reaction.
 
• It helps in the removal of a water molecule from ethanol to form ethene.
 
 
 
• **Ethene (Ethylene):**
 
 
• A colorless flammable gas with a faint "sweet and musky" odor.
 
• It is the simplest alkene and an important building block in the petrochemical industry.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ethene:**
 
 
• Ethene is widely used in the production of polymers such as polyethylene.
 
• It also plays a role in the ripening of fruits and is used as a plant hormone in agriculture.
